title: Chirped Stack with Graded Thickness
scientific_hypothesis: A chirped stack with systematically varying layer thicknesses will broaden the UV reflection band and improve SWIR transmission compared to uniform quarter-wave stacks.
design_principle: Chirped structures create multiple Bragg conditions across the stack, broadening the reflection band; grading thickness from substrate to air can improve impedance matching and reduce sideband reflection in the SWIR band.
proposed_topology: Air | (hfo2 | sio2)_10 with linearly chirped thickness | sio2 substrate | 20 layers total
manufacturing_considerations: Chirped deposition requires calibrated thickness monitoring
Linear chirp is simpler to implement than arbitrary grading
theory_basis: Chirped Bragg reflector theory for broadband reflection
Impedance matching through graded optical thickness
expected_advantages: Broader UV reflection band than quarter-wave stack
Potentially better SWIR transmission due to reduced sideband effects
Systematic design rule easier to manufacture than fully optimized stack
known_risks: Chirp parameters may not be optimal for this specific band combination
May require more layers to achieve same UV reflection as quarter-wave
Chirp direction (thick-to-thin vs thin-to-thick) affects performance
execution_request_english: Design a chirped multilayer stack on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Stack structure: Air | (hfo2 | SiO2 (Lemarchand))_10 with linearly chirped optical thickness from substrate to air | SiO2 (Lemarchand) substrate, totaling 20 layers. Optimize starting thickness, ending thickness, chirp direction, and chirp rate to maximize transmission in 1000-1700 nm band and reflection in 300-450 nm band. Use only hfo2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand) materials. Evaluate performance at normal incidence, unpolarized light.
